# tests/fixtures/gh/ — manifest

Hand-written `gh` fixtures that back the bats suite. Each fixture pairs with a
sibling `<name>.schema.json` capturing the **shape** (key paths and value
types) of real `gh` output for the equivalent `--json` query.
`tests/test_fixture_contract.bats` enforces that every key path used in a
fixture is present in its schema — so the next time `gh` evolves or a fixture
is hand-edited with a hallucinated key, CI fails instead of silently
green-lighting a broken predicate (see GH#8 for the canonical near-miss).

Schemas are regenerated by `tests/fixtures/gh/refresh.sh` against
`$LOOP_FIXTURE_REPO` (default: `aniryou/loop`). Run it any time you change
the `--json` field set on a runner query, or when CI's
`LOOP_FIXTURE_LIVE=1` test reports drift.

Last refreshed: **2026-05-07** (against `aniryou/loop`).

## Fixture map

| Fixture | Source `gh` command (production) | Scenario |
|---|---|---|
| `issues-high.json` | `gh issue list --repo $REPO --state open --label severity:high --json number,assignees --limit 50` | Two unassigned + one assigned; backs `eligibility_dev_count` and the assignee filter test in `test_eligibility.bats`. |
| `issues-medium.json` | `gh issue list --repo $REPO --state open --label severity:medium --json number,assignees --limit 50` | Different unassigned numbers from `issues-high.json` so the union-with-overlap test exercises `sort -u`. |
| `issues-with-locks.json` | `gh issue list --repo $REPO --state open --label severity:high --json number --limit 50` | Four issue numbers (101–104) used by the lock-dir post-filter test. Number-only shape (no `assignees`). |
| `prs-current.json` | `gh pr list --repo $REPO --state open --search "head:dev-agent/ -is:draft" --json number,commits,reviews --limit 100` | One PR whose `[reviewer-agent: clean]` review is *newer* than the head commit; the `eligibility_review_pending` jq filter must filter it OUT. |
| `prs-stale.json` | (same command) | One PR whose `[reviewer-agent: changes]` review is *older* than the head commit; the filter must INCLUDE it. |
| `prs-mixed.json` | (same command) | Three PRs covering current/stale/no-reviews so the filter returns 2. |
| `prs-dispatch.json` | `gh pr list --repo $REPO --state open --json number,headRefName,isDraft,mergeable --limit 100` | Six PRs covering every dispatcher branch: `dev-agent/*` non-draft / draft / conflicting, plus `feature/*` to verify branch-prefix filtering. |

## Schema notes

- Schemas use a flat dict shape: `{ "<jq-path>": "<type-union>" }`.
  - Path syntax: `.` for the root, `[]` for "any element of this array",
    `.foo` for an object field — so `.[].reviews[].submittedAt`.
  - Type names are jq's: `null`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `array`,
    `object`. Multiple types observed at the same path are joined with `|`.
- Schema source uses `--state all` and drops the `--label` filter so even
  repos where a label is currently empty still produce a representative
  schema. The fixture's *production* command is the column above; the
  schema-source command is encoded in `refresh.sh`.
- `null` in a fixture is always tolerated: scenarios often stub fields with
  `null` to scope what's relevant. The contract still rejects (a) keys not
  present in the schema (a hallucinated field) and (b) non-null types the
  schema doesn't list (e.g. a `string` where real gh always returns a
  `number`).

## Refresh workflow

```bash
# Default — regenerate schemas against aniryou/loop
tests/fixtures/gh/refresh.sh

# Different source repo (must have at least one open issue and PR)
LOOP_FIXTURE_REPO=octocat/hello-world tests/fixtures/gh/refresh.sh

# Live contract test — runs refresh.sh and asserts no git diff
LOOP_FIXTURE_LIVE=1 bats tests/test_fixture_contract.bats
```

`refresh.sh` is **read-only** (only `gh ... list` / `gh ... view`); it never
mutates the source repo. Running it twice in a row produces no `git diff`
unless the gh API shape itself has drifted.
